title: Employee Handbook
author: P036
summary: The Silvering Homes employee handbook: working hours, annual leave, sickness absence, hybrid working, lone working for field staff, vans and equipment, conduct, and where to find the full HR policies.

version_history.change: Hybrid working, lone working app and family-friendly updates
Added AI and Copilot use; updated sickness reporting for field staff

blocks.p: This handbook explains what you can expect from Silvering Homes as an employer and what we expect from you. It summarises our HR policies in plain English. The full policies are in **People, IT & Data > HR Policies**. If the handbook and a full policy differ, the full policy applies. If you have a question, ask your manager or the HR Business Partner, {{person:P036}}.
We employ {{fact:staff_count}} people, including {{fact:operatives_count}} operatives in the in-house repairs service based at the Aylesford depot.

bullets: Standard hours are **37 hours a week**, Monday to Friday, for office-based staff.
Office staff can use flexitime between 07:30 and 18:30, with core hours of 10:00-12:00 and 14:00-16:00. Up to two flexi days can be taken each month.
Operatives work 07:30-16:00 Monday to Thursday and 07:30-15:30 on Friday, with a 30-minute unpaid lunch break.
Operatives on the out-of-hours rota get a standby allowance of £35 a night (£55 at weekends and bank holidays), plus overtime at time and a half for call-outs, with a minimum of 2 hours.
Full-time staff get **27 days' annual leave plus bank holidays**, rising to **30 days after 5 years'** continuous service. Part-time staff get a pro rata entitlement in hours.
The leave year runs from 1 April to 31 March.
You can carry over up to **5 days** to the next leave year with your manager's approval. Carried-over leave must be used by 30 June.
Book leave in PeoplePath at least twice as far in advance as the length of the leave (for example, 2 weeks' notice for 1 week off).
Repairs operatives: no more than **two operatives from the same trade** may be on leave at the same time, and leave in July and August is allocated on a rota to protect repairs performance.
You can buy up to 5 extra days a year through salary sacrifice. Apply in March.

numbered: Phone your manager (not a text or email) before your start time on the first day, or by 08:00 if you are field-based so your jobs can be reallocated in FieldLoop.
Tell them why you are off and when you expect to be back.
Keep in touch on days 4 and 7 if you are still off.
From day 8 you need a fit note from your GP.

blocks.p: Your manager will hold a return to work conversation after every absence. A formal attendance review is triggered by **3 episodes or 8 working days in a rolling 12 months**, or any absence of 4 weeks or more (long-term absence). Reasonable adjustments and an Occupational Health referral are considered at every stage.

table.caption: Occupational sick pay (includes Statutory Sick Pay)

blocks.p: Office-based roles are hybrid. Most staff work at Kingsgate House for at least **two days a week**, with Tuesday as the team day for each directorate. Contact centre advisers follow the published rota. Hybrid working is a working arrangement, not a contractual right, and may change to meet service needs.

bullets: Work from a safe, private space. Do not take calls about residents where you can be overheard.
Complete the homeworking display screen equipment (DSE) self-assessment in PeoplePath. We will provide a monitor, keyboard and chair if needed.
Never print residents' personal data at home.
Hybrid working allowance: £10 a month, paid through payroll.

blocks.p: Housing officers, surveyors, operatives and SilverLiving staff often work alone in residents' homes. Your safety comes first: you can always leave a situation that feels unsafe.

numbered: **Check before you go.** Look at the Keystone warning markers for the address before every visit. Markers show a risk to staff (for example violence, aggressive dogs or hoarding). They do not show the reason in detail.
**Log in.** Start a visit on the SafeShift lone working app with the address and expected duration. Operatives' FieldLoop job start counts as the log-in.
**Check in.** If you go over the expected duration, the app prompts you. If you do not respond within 15 minutes it escalates to the monitoring centre, then to your manager.
**Red alert.** Press and hold the SOS button. The monitoring centre listens in and calls the police if needed. The code phrase 'Can you check the red file?' on a call means you need help.
**Double-up visits.** Addresses with a high-risk marker must be visited in pairs or with the police. Never enter a property where there is a warning marker for violence on your own.
**Log out** at the end of every visit and at the end of your working day.

blocks.callout: Operatives are never expected to carry out work in a home where they feel unsafe. Leave, tell the planners and make a note in FieldLoop. The job will be rebooked as a double-up visit.
blocks.title: Your right to leave

blocks.p: Operatives receive a liveried van, a fuel card and a mobile device. Vans may be taken home but must not be used for personal journeys. Vans are fitted with telematics for safety and route planning; data is not used for performance management except in an investigation, with notice. Report any accident in the van to the Fleet Coordinator within 24 hours.

bullets: Paid monthly on the 25th. Payslips are in PeoplePath.
Pension: defined contribution scheme with employer contributions of up to 8% when you pay 5% or more. Some colleagues who transferred from the council remain in the Local Government Pension Scheme.
Market supplements may be paid for hard-to-fill roles, reviewed annually.
Employee assistance programme: free, confidential counselling 24/7.
Professional subscriptions paid for roles that need them (for example CIH, RICS, CIPD, ACA).
Only use Silvering-approved AI tools (Microsoft 365 Copilot during the pilot). Do not paste residents' or colleagues' personal data into public AI tools.
You are responsible for anything you send or decide, even if Copilot drafted it. Check facts and figures against the source.
Copilot can only see what you can already see. If it shows you something you should not have access to, report it to the IT Service Desk straight away. Do not open or share it.
Never use AI to make decisions about residents' tenancies, vulnerability or eligibility.

blocks.p: We expect everyone to live our values: We care, We listen and act, We take pride, We own it. Treat residents and colleagues with respect. Gifts or hospitality from residents or contractors worth more than £25 must be declared in the gifts register. You must not accept any gift from a contractor during a procurement.

Attendance Management Policy
Flexible Working Policy (you can request flexible working from day one)
Family Leave Policy (maternity, paternity, adoption, shared parental and neonatal leave)

title: Trades Recruitment Report - Electricians and Damp & Mould Operatives
author: P013
summary: Executive Team paper on hard-to-fill trades vacancies: the vacancy position, recruitment campaign results, pay benchmarking, the proposed electrician market supplement, the impact on repairs and subcontractor costs, and the recommendations.

blocks.p: We have had **two electrician vacancies since March and May 2026** and one plasterer vacancy since June 2026. We have also struggled to recruit a third Operative Decorator (Damp & Mould). Three campaigns have produced only one appointable electrician, who turned down our offer for a contractor role paying £6,000 more. The vacancies are a major cause of the fall in routine repairs in target, from {{sql:SELECT routine_pct FROM monthly_repairs WHERE month='2025-10'}}% in October 2025 to {{sql:SELECT routine_pct FROM monthly_repairs WHERE month='2026-10'}}% in October 2026, and of higher spend on the Brightline Electrical subcontract.

table.caption: Table 1 - Trades establishment and staff in post (PeoplePath, 1 October 2026). Electrical includes only the operative electricians in Repairs; Damp & mould includes the plasterer post.

blocks.p: We currently have {{fact:ppl_electricians_in_post}} directly employed electricians, against an establishment of four. Rob Quinlan (Compliance Officer) is a qualified electrician but is not part of the repairs workforce.

Our electrician salary range is £36,000-£39,000. Local housing association and contractor rates for an approved electrician (18th Edition, AM2, with van) are £40,000-£45,000 for employed roles and £230-£260 a day for self-employed work. Exit interviews and candidate feedback cite pay, the 'on call' rota and van restrictions.

Brightline Electrical is paid about £168 per EICR and contract rates for repairs. At Month 6 subcontractor costs were about £95,000 over budget, partly offset by a £69,000 pay underspend. Each electrician vacancy costs roughly £18,000 a year more in subcontractor cost than an employed electrician, before the service impact.

numbered: Pay a **market supplement of £3,000 a year** to electricians (existing and new), reviewed annually against benchmarking.
Introduce a £1,000 referral bonus for trades roles (paid half at start, half after probation).
Take on two electrical apprentices from September 2027 with the local FE college.
Rewrite the job advert to lead with what matters to trades (pay, van, hours, kit, training) and shorten it.
Improve onboarding so that new operatives are productive within four weeks (shadowing, FieldLoop training, van stock).

blocks.callout: Recommendation 1 is subject to Executive Team approval. The market supplement is not in the 2026/27 budget.

title: Data Protection Guidance - Special Category Data and Vulnerability Information
author: P014
summary: How to collect, record, store and share special category data and vulnerability information about residents and staff, including Keystone vulnerability flags, sensitivity labels, SharePoint storage rules and Copilot.

blocks.p: We hold sensitive information about many residents to help us give them the right service: health conditions, disabilities, mental health, domestic abuse and support needs. In Keystone, {{sql:SELECT COUNT(*) FROM tenancies WHERE vulnerability_flag=1|int}} tenancies have a vulnerability flag. Most of this is **special category data** under UK GDPR (health, ethnicity, religion, sex life, sexual orientation, biometric and genetic data) or is similarly sensitive (domestic abuse, criminal offences). Losing or oversharing it can cause real harm and an ICO investigation.

We process vulnerability data under Article 6(1)(e) (public task) or (c) (legal obligation), and Article 9(2)(g) (substantial public interest) with the Data Protection Act 2018 Schedule 1 conditions for safeguarding and support for individuals with a particular disability or medical condition. Our appropriate policy document is in this library.

bullets: Record a vulnerability flag and type only where it affects how we deliver a service (for example a respiratory condition and damp and mould, a hearing impairment and contact method, or domestic abuse and the address being hidden).
Use the set categories. Free-text detail goes in the restricted Support Needs tab, which only housing officers, SilverLiving and the damp team can see.
Review each flag at every tenancy visit and at least every 2 years. Remove flags that no longer apply.
Never put vulnerability details in a FieldLoop job description. Operatives see the access note ('Call before arriving', 'Two-person visit') only.

rows: Everyday working documents without personal data
Personal data of residents or staff; commercial information
Restricted libraries or folders with named access
Special category data, vulnerability lists, salaries, disciplinary and ASB evidence
Only in libraries restricted to a named group; no external sharing; no 'People in your organisation' links
table.caption: Table 1 - Sensitivity labels

blocks.callout: Exports from Keystone that include vulnerability_type, health or domestic abuse data must be labelled Highly Confidential, stored only in the restricted Data Quality library, and deleted within 30 days. Never save them in general team libraries such as IT & Data or Recruitment.
blocks.title: Keystone exports

blocks.p: Copilot respects existing permissions: it can only use content that the person asking already has access to. It cannot tell whether a document is stored in the wrong place. If a vulnerability list is saved in a library that all staff can read, Copilot may surface it in anyone's answers. Before the pilot expands, the IT & Data team is running a search for files containing vulnerability terms and salary data in broadly shared locations.

Share special category data with partners (police, adult social care, the council) only under an information sharing agreement or a safeguarding duty, using secure email. Record what was shared, with whom and why on the case.

Report any actual or suspected breach to the Data Protection Officer (dpo@silvering-homes.org.uk) immediately, and within 24 hours at the latest. We must notify the ICO within 72 hours of becoming aware of a reportable breach.

title: IT Acceptable Use Policy
author: P014
summary: Rules for using Silvering's IT systems, devices, email, Teams, SharePoint and AI tools, including passwords and MFA, mobile devices for field staff, external sharing and monitoring.

blocks.p: This policy applies to all staff, board members, agency workers and contractors who use Silvering Homes IT, including laptops, mobile phones, FieldLoop devices, Microsoft 365 and line-of-business systems (Keystone, FieldLoop, Assure360, Northway Finance Cloud, PeoplePath).

bullets: Use a passphrase of at least 14 characters. Never share it or write it down.
Multi-factor authentication (Microsoft Authenticator) is mandatory for all accounts.
Lock your screen (Windows + L) whenever you leave your device.
Store work in SharePoint or Teams, not on your laptop's hard drive or a personal OneDrive.
Use 'Specific people' links when sharing. 'Anyone' links are disabled; 'People in your organisation' links must not be used for personal or sensitive data.
Apply the right sensitivity label to every document that contains personal data.
Check the recipients before sending, especially when the auto-complete suggests an external address.
Devices are managed by Intune and can be wiped remotely if lost. Report a lost device to the Service Desk within 1 hour.
Do not take photos of residents or their belongings unless they are needed for a repair or inspection. Store photos only in FieldLoop or Assure360, never in the camera roll.
Do not install unapproved apps.

blocks.p: Only Microsoft 365 Copilot (for licensed pilot users) is approved. Public AI chatbots must not be used with any Silvering information. See the Employee Handbook section 8.
We log use of our systems for security, and may review logs in an investigation. Monitoring is proportionate and in line with our privacy notice for staff.
Breaches may lead to disciplinary action. Report security incidents to the IT Service Desk (ext. 4400) straight away.

subject: Electrician market supplement - ExCo decision
summary: Lauren Hughes asks Simone Achterberg and Martin Okafor to approve the electrician market supplement; Daniel Kerr argues £3,000 is too low; the Executive Team agrees £4,500 on 3 November, superseding the recruitment report.

messages.body:
Simone, Martin,

Following the trades recruitment report (attached), can we get a decision on the electrician market supplement at ExCo on 3 November? We have interviews for the third electrician campaign this week and I'd like to be able to make an offer with the supplement included.

The report recommends £3,000 a year for all electricians, existing and new. Two electricians are in post now, so the cost is £6,000 a year now and £12,000 at full establishment, plus on-costs.

Lauren

Lauren,

Thanks for pushing this. Honestly, £3k won't do it. The candidate we lost in May went for £6k more, and the two lads I've got are being phoned by agencies every week. If one of them goes, we're at one electrician and Brightline will be doing half our electrical work.

I'd say £4,500 minimum. It's still cheaper than one month of Brightline overspend.

Dan

Both,

I can fund it in year from the pay underspend, so 2026/27 isn't the problem. It goes into the 2027/28 budget as a permanent cost, and with interest cover where it is I want it reviewed annually and tied to vacancies being filled.

I'm comfortable with £4,500 if it comes with a review clause and if we can show a reduction in Brightline spend within six months.

Martin

All,

ExCo agreed this morning: **market supplement of £4,500 a year** for all electricians (existing and new) from 1 December 2026, reviewed annually against benchmarking, and conditional on a six-monthly report on Brightline spend. The £3,000 in the October report is superseded.

Lauren - please update the offer letters, the job advert and the JD wording, and let Dev know so the pay file reflects the decision. Can you also make sure that pay file isn't sitting somewhere everyone can see? Craig flagged it at the Copilot steering group.

Simone

title: Copilot Pilot - Champions
summary: The Copilot champions share prompts and wins and report oversharing: salary data and a vulnerability export surfacing in Copilot answers, a recap that got an action wrong, and tips for Excel.

messages.text: Morning champions! Licences are live for all 40 pilot users. Please post your wins, your fails and anything weird here. Remember: if Copilot shows you something you shouldn't see, don't open it or share it - tell me.
First win: asked Copilot to build a timeline of a damp complaint from the emails and the repairs history. Took 4 minutes instead of an hour. It did miss one appointment, so I still checked FieldLoop.

Excel tip: 'Explain the three biggest variances in the I&E sheet and suggest commentary' works well on the management accounts. But it called a favourable cost variance 'adverse' once because of the sign convention. Tell it the convention in the prompt!

Um, slightly worrying. I asked Copilot 'what are the pay bands for operatives' and the answer listed actual named salaries for the electricians and some of the managers. Reference was a file called 'Pay Bands and Salaries 2026-27' in People > Recruitment. I didn't open it.

Thanks Sophie, that's exactly what we want reported. That file is labelled Confidential but it's in a library all staff can read. Logging it as oversharing incident 1. Dev/Lauren - can you move it to the restricted HR Pay folder?
Sorry, my fault - I saved it there while I was writing the recruitment report. Will move it tomorrow.

Another one, I think. Asked Copilot to 'summarise vulnerable households at Brenchley Gardens so I can plan winter visits'. It gave me a list with names, phone numbers and conditions like mental health and domestic abuse survivor, from 'Keystone data quality check - vulnerability flags' in IT & Data. Useful for me, but I'm not sure everyone should be able to see that?

Ugh, that's mine. It's a data quality export I ran on 7 Oct. It should have been in the restricted Data Quality library and labelled Highly Confidential. Incident 2. I'll sort it today and run a content search for other exports.

Thanks both for flagging this quickly. This is the main risk we worried about. Craig, please bring a full list to the steering group on the 29th. Amira, please use the restricted Support Needs view in Keystone for your visit planning.
Teams recap of our Castlemere site meeting is great, but it gave the as-builts action to me instead of Castlemere. Always check the owners!

Awaab's Law written summaries: I paste my inspection notes into Word and ask Copilot to draft the summary in plain English using the template headings. Down from 45 minutes to about 15. I still check every date and the works start date by hand.
Update: I haven't moved the pay file yet - I don't have permission to the HR Pay folder. Raised a ticket. 🙄
Will grant it today. I moved and relabelled the Keystone export on the 21st... actually, let me double-check, it's still showing in search for me. Hmm. Looking into it.
Is there a prompt for 'is this repair an emergency?' I keep checking the policy manually.
Good idea for the champions session - we could build a little repairs priorities agent in Copilot Studio grounded on the repairs policy. Adding to Thursday's agenda.

summary: Steering group reviews the first four weeks of the Copilot pilot: usage and time saved, three oversharing incidents (salary file, vulnerability export, board paper link), the permissions review gap and the decision on extending the pilot.
agenda: Extension to 60 users and 2027/28 budget bid

transcript.text: Afternoon all. Thanks for coming. We've got an hour, and I want to spend most of it on the oversharing incidents, because that's the thing that would stop this pilot. Craig, can you start with the headline numbers?

Sure. Can everyone see my screen? ... Okay. Forty licences, all forty completed Essentials before they got a licence. Thirty-one weekly active users, so seventy-eight per cent. Self-reported time saved is about two hours a week each, from the pulse survey, but that's only twenty-six responses.
Self-reported. I'd want something harder before I put money in the budget.
Agreed. We've got before-and-after timings for Awaab's Law summaries from Ellie and the complaints team. Summaries went from about forty-five minutes to fifteen.
And stage 1 drafts are quicker too. Owen, is that right?
Yeah. Mark's doing timelines in a few minutes. Quality's good, but it misses things if the information's only in FieldLoop, because Copilot can't see FieldLoop.
Okay. Oversharing. Craig.

Three incidents. One: Sophie asked about pay bands and got named salaries from a working file in the People Recruitment library. Two: Amira got a list of vulnerable households with conditions, from a Keystone export I saved in IT and Data. Three: a draft board paper was shared with an 'everyone in the organisation' link.
The board paper was the September performance report. I've removed the link.
Thanks Joanne. And the other two?

So, um, this is slightly embarrassing. I thought I'd moved the Keystone export on the twenty-first, but I'd only copied it to the restricted library. The original's still in IT and Data. I'll delete it straight after this meeting.
And the pay file is still in Recruitment. Dev couldn't get into the HR Pay folder, there was a ticket...
That's done now, I granted it yesterday.
Okay, so it can move today.
Can I just say, the point here is these aren't Copilot problems. They're our filing problems. Copilot's just made them visible.
Exactly. Copilot only shows you what you can already see. Anybody could have found that file through SharePoint search.
Which is why I'm not comfortable expanding until we've reviewed every site, not just three. Craig, which ones are left?

Finance, Development, Repairs, Assets and the hub. We did Board, People and Neighbourhoods in September. Ironically, both incidents were on the People site, which we'd reviewed, because the files were added afterwards.
So a one-off review isn't enough. We need something ongoing.
Yes. I'm proposing a weekly content search for sensitive terms, vulnerability, salary, NI number, that sort of thing, plus auto-labelling for Keystone exports. I need about two days a month for it.
Fine. Let's make it a condition. Sophie, you reported the first one. How did it feel as a user?
Honestly, a bit scary. It was just there in the answer. I didn't know if I'd done something wrong.
You didn't. You did exactly the right thing. Let's put that in the training: what it looks like and what to do.
I'll add it to the Essentials module and the managers' session.
Great. Extension. The proposal is sixty users in January, about sixteen thousand a year for the extra licences. Martin?

I'm not going to approve it today. Put it in as a 2027/28 budget bid for the seventeenth of November, with the time-saving evidence and the permissions review done. And interest cover is tight, so it'll be competing with damp and mould.
That's fair. So the decision is: no extension yet; bid at the budget kick-off; full permissions review first. Is everyone okay with that?
Yes.
Yes. And I'd like the board to get a short update in December. They'll ask about data protection.
Good shout. Okay, Craig, Lauren, actions please. Let's move the files today. Thanks everyone.

recap.summary: In the first four weeks, 31 of 40 pilot users were active weekly and reported saving about two hours a week; there are firm timings for Awaab's Law summaries (45 down to 15 minutes). Three oversharing incidents were reviewed: the pay bands file with named salaries in People > Recruitment, a Keystone vulnerability export in IT & Data, and a board paper with an organisation-wide link. Only the board paper link has been fixed. The group decided not to extend the pilot yet. A full permissions review and ongoing content searches are now conditions, and the extension goes forward as a 2027/28 budget bid.

topics.title: Results
topics.text: 78% weekly active; about 2 hours a week self-reported time saving; Finance wants harder evidence.

topics.title: Oversharing
topics.text: Three incidents, all caused by where content was stored. The Keystone export was copied, not moved, so the original is still in IT & Data. The pay file is still in Recruitment; access to the HR Pay folder was granted on 28 October.

topics.title: Permissions review
topics.text: Finance, Development, Repairs, Assets and hub sites are not yet reviewed. Weekly content search and auto-labelling proposed.

topics.title: Extension
topics.text: No extension yet. Bid for 20 more licences (about £16,200 a year) at the 17 November budget kick-off.

decisions: Do not extend the pilot until all sites have had a permissions review.
Make a weekly sensitive-content search and auto-labelling of Keystone exports a condition of the pilot continuing.
Submit the licence extension as a 2027/28 budget bid.

actions.action: Delete the original Keystone vulnerability export from IT & Data
Move the pay bands and salaries file to the restricted HR Pay folder and relabel it Highly Confidential
Complete permissions review of the Finance, Development, Repairs, Assets and hub sites
Add 'what to do if Copilot shows you something sensitive' to Essentials and the managers' session
Prepare the 2027/28 budget bid for Copilot licences with time-saving evidence
Copilot pilot update for the December Board
